Why you can trust the numbers

One column is the answer. Three look like it.

The royalty export returns 15 uppercase columns. Metric 6 is the last one.

ColumnWhat it actually isJul 2026
ANRM TANDEM TQL REVENUE Revenue, not royalty — 2.5× too big $1,090,238.70
ANRM TANDEM TQL ROYALTY EVENTS Says “royalty” — but it is an event count 624,384
TANDEM TQLS A count of TQLs, not dollars 520,000
✓ TANDEM TQL ROYALTIES The dollar royalty figure $435,996.19
The two count columns are harmless — nobody mistakes 624,384 for dollars. The dangerous one is REVENUE: wrong by 2.5×, and still a perfectly plausible dollar amount to paste into a fund doc.

So the skill pins the ratio too: royalties are 0.3999 of revenue in all 28 months. One division catches a wrong-column read.

Why you can trust the numbers

The rest of the guards

  • Validated baselines are checked in. July 2026 values for every metric live in the skill file. A rebuild that cannot reproduce them is known-wrong before anyone reads the output.
  • The month-end / month-start trap. Metrics 1–5 anchor on 2026-07-01; the royalty row is dated 2026-07-31. Take the neighbouring row and you divide last month’s dollars by this month’s pages — a PPR that looks entirely reasonable and is wrong.
  • Low-base marketplaces get flagged. JP sits at 0.1% on ALC GMS, where a single 0.1pp move reads as −50% MoM and −50% YoY at once. Arithmetically right, analytically meaningless — so anything under ~1% must be marked not comparable.
  • MoM and YoY are relative changes, not point deltas. 10.8% against 10.2% is “+5.9% higher”, not “+0.6 points”. Different claims about the same pair of numbers.

The mandated SQL is held verbatim. Month-over-month comparability of the fund doc depends on the definition not drifting, so the skill forbids adjusting it mid-run to make a number look more plausible. And Tandem PPR is not KDPS PPR — different programmes, different rates, guarded because it is an easy and expensive mistake.

Each skill also carries its open questions, addressed to the section owner — 7 on Section 5, 4 on KDPS Health. Unresolved issues are checked in, not smoothed over.

How it's wired

Read-only by construction, not by instruction

QuickSight answers failing while SQL answers keep working means the Kerberos ticket — not a broken dashboard.

Kerberos tickets

Every QuickSight-backed answer failing — with no signal at all.

Fixed by hand, with a password prompt. Needs doing again tomorrow.

Transferable

Design principles that transfer

  • Read-only by construction. Enforce it in the credential and the tool, never in the prompt.
  • Skills encode verification, not steps. A baseline and a magnitude range catch what a procedure cannot.
  • Hand off, never stall. If a query runs long, hand over the SQL and the link. A partial answer with a link beats a silent agent.
  • Fight the model's instincts in the payload. Every spreadsheet-mcp response carries a "post the entire table" contract, because it summarizes otherwise — plus row and column counts so it can self-audit.
  • Guard cells over trust. A view asserts B17 == "WW" and warns if the export was for a different selection.
  • Hold confidential data for as little time as possible. The Finance Model expires from the bucket after 21 days and every cached copy is owner-only on disk. The capability lapsing is the intended trade, not a defect.
  • Check in the open questions, addressed to a named owner.

Where it's fragile

What needs fixing

GapThe failure it causes
Single host, single credential set, 4 usersEvery query is attributed to me; access can't grow
Skills deploy by manual scp, no reverse pathRepo and host drift both ways
Patches re-applied on every installA toolbox update silently reverts multi-user access
Pinned by a global update pauseNo other toolbox tool auto-updates either
Guardian leaks its lock into tmuxGoes silent right after a restart it performed — hid a 6-day outage
No Kerberos renewal automationQuickSight answers break roughly daily
Finance Model must be re-uploaded every 21 daysLifecycle deletes it by design; nothing alerts when the window lapses

Three of these showed up today: the missing Kerberos ticket, the Finance Model having aged out of the bucket, and the repo/host drift.

The ask

Three things

  • A home that isn't one person's desktop. A service account or dedicated host with per-user auth — so the allowlist grows past four and queries aren't all attributed to one alias.
  • Deployed skills and real health monitoring. Deployment shouldn't be scp, and a system that fails invisibly needs a heartbeat. The guardian's top-ranked fix is one line.
  • From this room: co-sign that the value is real — and bring your own recurring work. The fund doc is covered end to end now, and the shape is deliberately reusable: a metric table, a month parameter, the mandated query held verbatim, caveats, and open questions.
It's been up two weeks straight and it produces four of the five sections of the fund doc, plus the appendix. It also has no owner but me, no monitoring, and one expired ticket between it and half its capability. That's the ask.
